articles.title: LemFi amplia serviços financeiros para brasileiros que vivem no exterior | G1
articles.standfirst: Plataforma reúne transferências internacionais, poupança, crédito e internet móvel em um aplicativo; dinheiro pode ser enviado ao Brasil via PIX.
articles.summary: Plataforma reúne transferências internacionais, poupança, crédito e internet móvel em um aplicativo; dinheiro pode ser enviado ao Brasil via PIX.
articles.body:
A LemFi , plataforma financeira voltada a pessoas que vivem e constroem suas vidas em diferentes países, anunciou a maior expansão de produtos de sua história. A empresa apresentou uma nova identidade global, com o slogan “Ambition has no passport” — em tradução livre, “A ambição não tem passaporte” - e um aplicativo reformulado para reunir diferentes serviços financeiros em uma única plataforma.

LemFi, plataforma financeira com soluções para brasileiros — Foto: Divulgação

A novidade para a comunidade brasileira no exterior é a possibilidade de enviar dinheiro ao Brasil por meio do Pix, sem tarifa de transferência, segundo a companhia. A plataforma também reúne serviços de transferências internacionais e amplia seu portfólio com opções de poupança e crédito no Reino Unido, além de um serviço de internet móvel por eSIM em mais de 150 países.

A brasileira Isa Testa é responsável pela LemFi na América Latina — Foto: Divulgação

Em entrevista, a brasileira Isa Testa, responsável pela área de América Latina da LemFi, destacou a importância dos brasileiros que vivem fora do país para a empresa. “A comunidade brasileira que vive no exterior é muito importante para a LemFi. São pessoas que constroem novas oportunidades em outros países, mas continuam mantendo vínculos afetivos e financeiros com o Brasil, apoiando familiares e permanecendo presentes na vida de quem ficou” , diz a executiva.

Segundo Isa, muitos brasileiros precisam administrar compromissos financeiros em dois países ao mesmo tempo. “Cada vez mais, brasileiros no exterior estão construindo vidas em dois lugares simultaneamente. Eles vivem fora enquanto ajudam a construir uma vida para amigos e familiares que ficaram aqui. Nosso trabalho é fazer com que a movimentação do dinheiro seja uma preocupação a menos, com soluções financeiras acessíveis e adequadas à realidade dessas pessoas, apoiando a realização de suas ambições” .

A principal mudança é a integração de diferentes serviços em um único aplicativo. Além das transferências internacionais, a plataforma passa a oferecer produtos de poupança e crédito para clientes elegíveis no Reino Unido. O serviço de eSIM permite contratar pacotes de dados móveis para usar a internet durante viagens internacionais.

De acordo com a empresa, o aplicativo foi reconstruído para facilitar o acesso aos produtos e permitir a inclusão de novos serviços conforme a operação se expande.

A disponibilidade varia de acordo com o país. As opções de poupança e crédito anunciadas na expansão são destinadas inicialmente ao mercado britânico, sem confirmação de lançamento desses produtos para residentes brasileiros.

Como funciona o envio de dinheiro ao Brasil?

Ridwan Olalere é cofundador e CEO da LemFi — Foto: Divulgação

A LemFi foi criada para facilitar transferências internacionais, especialmente para pessoas que vivem longe de seus países de origem e continuam enviando recursos para familiares e amigos.

Segundo a companhia, o dinheiro pode chegar ao Brasil por meio do Pix, sem tarifa de transferência. A empresa também afirma que o serviço permite movimentar recursos entre países de maneira rápida.

A disponibilidade das transferências, os métodos de pagamento e as condições aplicáveis dependem do país de origem, das regras locais e das opções apresentadas no aplicativo. Antes de concluir uma operação, o usuário deve conferir a taxa de câmbio, o valor final recebido e eventuais custos informados na plataforma.

Conta de poupança oferece rendimento no Reino Unido

Entre os novos produtos está a conta LemFi Instant Access Savings, destinada ao mercado britânico. Segundo a empresa, a conta oferece uma taxa promocional de 5% ao ano, pela métrica britânica AER, nos primeiros seis meses após a abertura.

Depois desse período, a taxa passa a ser de 3,04% ao ano, variável e vinculada à taxa básica de juros do Banco da Inglaterra. A conta pode ser aberta com depósito inicial de 1 libra e permite saques sem penalidade, conforme as condições divulgadas pela companhia.

Os depósitos são mantidos pela ClearBank e, segundo a empresa, contam com proteção do Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS), sistema britânico de proteção financeira, de até 120 mil libras por depositante elegível.

A conta é destinada a clientes elegíveis no Reino Unido e não está disponível para pessoas que não sejam residentes no país. Portanto, as condições anunciadas não representam uma oferta de poupança automaticamente disponível para brasileiros que vivem no Brasil..

A expansão inclui uma linha de crédito rotativa no Reino Unido, sujeita à disponibilidade e aos critérios de elegibilidade. O serviço é oferecido pela LemFi Credit, em parceria com a Pillar, empresa de crédito regulada pela autoridade financeira britânica Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), adquirida pela LemFi em 2025.

A linha poderá ser acessada com um cartão virtual compatível com Apple Pay e Google Pay. Clientes elegíveis também poderão consultar gratuitamente sua pontuação de crédito da Equifax diretamente no aplicativo.

A proposta é atender pessoas que se mudam para outro país e precisam construir um novo histórico financeiro, já que seu histórico de crédito e relacionamento bancário nem sempre são reconhecidos fora do país de origem.

eSIM permite acessar internet em mais de 150 países

Outra novidade é o serviço de eSIM, tecnologia que permite utilizar dados móveis no celular sem a necessidade de substituir o chip físico do aparelho.

De acordo com a LemFi, os usuários podem contratar um pacote de internet antes de chegar ao destino e evitar a dependência exclusiva do roaming internacional da operadora de origem ou a necessidade de comprar um chip local.

A cobertura anunciada abrange mais de 150 países. A disponibilidade e as condições dos pacotes podem variar conforme o destino e o plano contratado.

Por que a empresa está ampliando os serviços?

A expansão está relacionada ao perfil de clientes que vivem entre diferentes países, trabalham no exterior e mantêm compromissos financeiros em mais de uma região.

No anúncio, a LemFi cita uma estimativa de 304 milhões de pessoas vivendo fora do país onde nasceram e cerca de US$ 905 bilhões enviados internacionalmente por ano. Os números são apresentados pela empresa para contextualizar o mercado em que atua.

“Começamos a LemFi porque enviar dinheiro para casa era um processo problemático. O que aprendemos é que o desafio mais difícil começa depois da transferência” , conta Ridwan Olalere, cofundador e CEO da companhia.

Segundo o executivo, muitos clientes constroem carreiras e negócios em um país enquanto continuam apoiando pessoas em outro. A empresa afirma que pretende desenvolver serviços financeiros mais adequados a essa realidade.

A ampliação do portfólio vem acompanhada de uma nova identidade de marca, apresentada sob o conceito “Ambition has no passport”. A mensagem procura destacar a trajetória de pessoas que constroem carreiras, empresas, famílias e patrimônio em diferentes países.

A nova identidade será aplicada ao aplicativo, ao site, às ações de marketing e aos canais de redes sociais da companhia nos mercados em que atua.

“Nossos clientes não são definidos pelo país que deixaram. São definidos pelo que estão construindo” , afirma Isabel Ron-Pedrique, vice-presidente de Design e Marca da LemFi, em comunicado.

Fundada em 2021 por Ridwan Olalere e Rian Cochran, a LemFi é uma plataforma financeira voltada a pessoas que vivem ou mantêm vínculos financeiros entre diferentes países. O negócio começou com transferências internacionais e agora busca ampliar o portfólio de serviços.

A empresa afirma atender mais de dois milhões de clientes e movimentar mais de US$ 2 bilhões por mês em transações, com transferências para o Brasil e mais de 30 países da África, Ásia, Europa e outras regiões.

A LemFi também informa ter captado mais de US$ 85 milhões em investimentos de fundos como Highland Europe, Left Lane Capital, Palm Drive Capital e Endeavor Catalyst, além da aceleradora Y Combinator.

Com a expansão, a companhia pretende reunir transferências, poupança, crédito e conectividade em uma única plataforma, com serviços disponibilizados gradualmente conforme os mercados e as condições de elegibilidade.

articles.title: P&G beats estimates as price hikes haven't hurt demand yet
articles.summary: P&G earnings surprise despite macro pressures.
articles.body:
Procter & Gamble's ( PG ) price hikes aren't crushing a consumer base dealing with higher inflation, yet.

The Tide maker delivered sales and profit upside for its fiscal first quarter on Thursday. The company maintained its full-year sales and profit outlooks.

"The US consumer is remarkably resilient," P&G CFO Andre Schulten told Yahoo Finance.

Schulten said the business is being powered by higher income households, while the lower end is being more cautious.

P&G shares rose 2% in pre-market trading.

Net sales: $23.28 billion, +4% from the prior year vs. $22.82 billion estimate

Organic sales growth: +4% vs. +1.96% estimate Beauty segment organic revenue growth: +5.4% vs. +3.58% estimate Grooming segment organic revenue growth: +4.5% vs. +0.7% estimate Healthcare segment organic revenue growth: +2.7% vs. +2.51% estimate Fabric and home care segment organic revenue growth: +4.8% vs. +2.35% estimate Baby, feminine, and family care segment organic revenue growth: +3% vs. +0.99% estimate

Organic sales growth: +4% vs. +1.96% estimate

Beauty segment organic revenue growth: +5.4% vs. +3.58% estimate

Grooming segment organic revenue growth: +4.5% vs. +0.7% estimate

Healthcare segment organic revenue growth: +2.7% vs. +2.51% estimate

Fabric and home care segment organic revenue growth: +4.8% vs. +2.35% estimate

Baby, feminine, and family care segment organic revenue growth: +3% vs. +0.99% estimate

Adjusted earnings per share: $2.00, +1% from the prior year vs. $1.89 estimate

What else caught our attention: A sustained outlook

P&G reiterated organic sales growth of 1% to 3% for its fiscal year.

For the year, earnings are still expected to range from $6.89 to $7.11. Analysts were looking for fiscal year 2027 organic revenue growth of 2.19% and core earnings per share of $6.98.

articles.title: Norwegians Leave Gold in Forest as Some Fall for Scam
articles.summary: Swindlers have persuaded Norwegians into buying gold and leaving it in the forest as part of a growing investment fraud, according to the country’s banking l...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Swindlers have persuaded Norwegians into buying gold and leaving it in the forest as part of a growing investment fraud, according to the country's banking lobby.

"Several" bank clients have spent "large sums" to purchase gold and then left it out in nature, following promises that "others will keep it safe while the value rises," Finans Norge said in a statement Thursday, without specifying the amounts.

It said the scheme is one of three fraud methods that banks are "specifically warning against right now."

Last year, the losses of Norwegian lenders and their customers from financial fraud totaled 962 million kroner ($100 million), the lobby group said. At the same time, the banks prevented fraud attempts amounting to over 3.5 billion kroner.

articles.title: Meta's new nonvoting shares create an overhang — and Wall Street wants it gone
articles.summary: Meta should move fast on its new share sale, Wall Street says.
articles.body:
Meta ( META ) has created a new overhang on its stock that Wall Street wasn't expecting when it established a new class of stock.

The Street's advice to Mark Zuckerberg and his team: Issue the stock fast so the focus can return to the clear product momentum the company is enjoying with its new Muse AI agent .

"The sooner the better in our view as it would remove the overhang and the Street now knows it will have non-voting shares in Jan'27, and Meta can still do a substantial equity raise before then without even coming close to impacting Mark's voting control," JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth said.

Meta announced late Wednesday that it is establishing a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, which effectively serves as a 2-for-1 stock split.

Under the scheme — in part designed to keep founder Mark Zuckerberg working in California as the 5% billionaire's tax looms — existing shareholders will receive one new nonvoting Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they hold. Trading is slated to begin in January 2027.

Issuing nonvoting stock allows Zuckerberg to raise external capital for Meta's AI build-out without diluting his personal voting control over the tech giant.

The news took some air out of the balloon on what was an impressive quarter for Meta amid signs that its AI investments are paying off.

Meta's core advertising business reported a 26% increase in total revenue to $64.6 billion, powered by AI-driven recommendations, higher ad volume, and rising ad prices.

GAAP earnings per share came in at $3.83 versus analyst estimates of $3.56.

Meta stock fell 2% in premarket trading on Thursday.

"Net/net, some near-term noise in Meta shares, but we're encouraged by core Advertising and Meta's outlook for strong overall revenue growth in 2027, and the path to superintelligence is increasingly clear w/the Muse series of models & products," Anmuth said.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo hits stores Friday amid limited supplies
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo goes on sale Friday, but in-store supplies will be limited.
articles.body:
Apple's ( AAPL ) iPhone Duo goes on sale Friday, but you may be hard-pressed to get your hands on one.

Preorders for the company's first foldable smartphone sold out almost immediately last week, with delivery times pushed out well into late January.

As for getting a Duo on launch day, either you're already in line at an Apple Store, or you'll need to get extremely lucky.

The company said that while it has allocated some supply for walk-in customers, it expects that supply to sell out quickly.

"On Friday morning, our teams look forward to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to experience iPhone Duo and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves," Apple said in a statement.

"Apple Stores will have limited iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, and we're working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible."

At least some of the preorder madness comes down to scalpers hawking the foldable iPhone on sites like eBay at a stiff markup.

While the iPhone Duo starts at $1,999, sellers are asking for upwards of $4,000 for the pricey smartphone.

The Duo is one of Apple's most anticipated products in years. The biggest update to the company's most important device since it launched in 2007, the iPhone Duo could help raise the iPhone's average selling price, boosting Apple's bottom line.

The iPhone represented $209.58 billion of Apple's $416.16 billion in total revenue in 2025. That's well ahead of the company's second-largest business segment, Services, which brought in $109.15 billion.

The Duo also comes as Apple revamps its iPhone release schedule. Rather than debuting its full lineup of phones at its annual September event last month, Apple revealed only its top-tier smartphones, including the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.

The company is widely expected to unveil its standard iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 early next year. That should help even out the lumpiness in Apple's seasonal sales and provide a clearer picture of which devices consumers are purchasing.

Email Daniel Howley at dhowley@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on Twitter at @DanielHowley .

articles.title: Elon Musk says Tesla's Optimus robot needs to learn like a toddler
articles.summary: The Tesla CEO offered a fresh reminder that getting Optimus to behave like a human is no easy task.
articles.body:
Tesla ( TSLA ) CEO Elon Musk reminded investors this past summer that making thumbs for the Optimus humanoid robot would be no easy task.

Now he's out with a fresh reminder that getting Optimus to behave like a human out in the wild is also no easy task. Two reminders in under six months will likely cause Wall Street to dial back its sales estimates for Optimus in the medium term.

It appears Tesla is doing something similar — pulling back its $25 billion full-year capital expenditures commitment to $20 billion to ensure the humanoids the company delivers are highly usable.

"A big difference with Optimus versus the cars is we don't have this vast fleet of cars from which we can gather training data," Musk said on his late Wednesday earnings call . "With Optimus, we have to bootstrap it by making the robots and having them do self-play, which is really how a human learns to navigate the world. You can see this when you have a toddler, and they grow up, and initially, they're sort of wobbly, and they don't know how to do things. Eventually they learn to wipe their own ass, which is a big milestone. As anyone who's had kids knows. Then they learn to read and do all sorts of things and be able to do these things. They learn this by playing. We actually need Optimus to play at scale in order to have it be really good at tasks in the real world."

Tesla ended production of its flagship Model S and Model X vehicles at its Fremont, Calif., factory this past spring, specifically to make room for Optimus humanoid robot production — a stunning strategic pivot that tells you how all-in Musk is on this program.

The latest version, Optimus V3, stands 5'8" tall, weighs 125 pounds, runs on Tesla's new AI5 chip with roughly five times the memory bandwidth of its predecessor, and is powered by xAI's Grok for voice.

Production began at the Fremont factory in the summer. About 1,000 Gen 3 units are already operating on Tesla's live production floor.

"Musk tempered Optimus timeline expectations to over a year to reach the 1 million unit weekly run-rate," William Blair analyst Jed Dorsheimer said. "Early production has begun on the old Model S/X footprint in Fremont, but the critical hand and finger design are still being optimized. Data is not the bottleneck; real-world reps on open-ended tasks are. Musk noted the first applications will be in dangerous industrial applications by the end of 2027, and reaching people's homes sometime after. We think this was appropriately cautious and reinforces our view that Optimimus can remain important to the multiple well before it has meaningful impact on estimates."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: KFC switches to Coke. But Pepsi’s still king at Taco Bell
articles.summary: KFC dumped PepsiCo last week, but its sister chain Taco Bell announced Thursday it’s keeping the Mountain Dew Baja Blast maker on for another decade.
articles.body:
KFC dumped PepsiCo last week, but its sister chain Taco Bell announced Thursday it's keeping the Mountain Dew Baja Blast maker on for another decade.

The Taco Bell deal is a much-needed win for PepsiCo, whose business has had rough few weeks. Not only did it lose its longstanding contract with KFC to rival Coca-Cola, but its drink business in North America is also in a slump.

The company reported a 2% decline for its North America beverage unit during its most recent quarter, and its CEO Ramon Laguarta bluntly said on its earnings call that it's "not competing well in soft drinks," including newly acquired Poppi brand.

Losing the KFC contract is a blow for PepsiCo, considering it once owned the fried chicken chain. But keeping Taco Bell is a bigger deal, since the latter has generated $17 billion in US system-wide sales last year compared to KFC's roughly $5 billion. (Both chains are owned by Yum! Brands.)

Taco Bell and PepsiCo said in a statement that the two will continue collaborating on new beverages and foods until 2036, including upcoming new flavors for their Doritos Locos Tacos. It also noted that the Baja Blast drink has become a $1 billion brand.

As food prices rise and consumers look to cut back, the beverage category is a key growth area for Taco Bell and other fast food chains.

Taco Bell is aggressively expanding its beverage sales aiming to generate $5 billion in revenue by 2030. Last year, the chain released a lineup of "Refrescas" drinks aimed at attracting consumers searching for a beverage between meals. Further expansion will come from developing new Baja Blast options with Pepsi, including a limited-time pink lemonade with singer Olivia Rodrigo.

"Taco Bell's Baja Blast lineup has often been a key differentiator for the brand, and leaning into product exclusives can help drive visitation to quick service restaurant chains," Elizabeth Lafontaine, director of research at location analytics firm Placer.ai, previously told CNN.

"Especially as the industry faces steeper competition and consumers who are on the hunt for more value from fast food offerings," she added.

Taco Bell and PepsiCo said in a statement that they plan to stay ahead on "emerging beverage trends across crafted, functional and energy beverages, including energy offerings designed to appeal to Gen Z consumers and unlock new morning and afternoon occasions."

Taco Bell has been a bright spot in the fast food industry, but saw a traffic decline over the summer due toa cyclospora outbreak that was linked to lettuce served at a number of restaurants. The company will give a fuller view of the sales impact when it releases earnings next month.

articles.title: Mortgage rates dropped for the first time in months
articles.summary: The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.32% this week.
articles.body:
Mortgage rates fell for the first time in over two months, though they remain not far off from multiyear highs.

The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.32% this week through Wednesday, down from 7.4% a week earlier, according to Freddie Mac data.

Treasury yields, which mortgage rates closely track, eased slightly this week as investors fled to safe-haven assets amid growing political and economic unrest in Europe.

Despite very slight rate relief, home buyers are staying on the sidelines. Mortgage applications for new home purchases dropped 7% through Friday from a week earlier, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association.

"The housing market continues to face significant headwinds as elevated mortgage rates and affordability pressures keep many prospective buyers on the sidelines," MBA president and CEO Bob Broeksmit said in a statement.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS biz as shares; 30,000 certificates affected
articles.summary: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business after weak-key incident; 30,000 certificates affected, shares slide 36% as CERT-In flags flaw.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Shares of digital trust company eMudhra plunged 20% on BSE for the second consecutive day on Thursday after the company announced its decision to voluntarily exit the global SSL/TLS (Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security) certificate business following a security incident involving eight of its intermediate certificate authorities.The company’s board decided to withdraw from the business after reviewing its commercial prospects and the scrutiny triggered by the incident. The global SSL/TLS business contributes about 1% of eMudhra’s revenue, but rising compliance requirements, increasing costs and competition from free certificate providers have reduced its potential returns, the company said.“The scrutiny was disproportionate to the revenue contribution of the business,” Kaushik Srinivasan, co-founder of eMudhra, told TOI, explaining the board’s decision. He said the board met on Thursday to assess the business’s future following the incident and the sharp fall in the company’s share price over the past two sessions.Investors were bearish on the eMudhra stock after the cyber incident. In two sessions since the incident, its stock price has crashed 36% to Rs 345 by Thursday’s close, from Rs 539 at Monday’s close.The issue was reported on Oct 17 by Dennis Jackson, a member of Mozilla’s cryptography engineering team, who flagged weaknesses in the keys associated with the eight eMudhra intermediate certificates.Srinivasan said the economics of the business were becoming less attractive as certificate validity periods shortened. “The return on investment, considering the effort, investment and compliance requirements, is becoming less attractive. It makes more sense to strengthen and invest in our enterprise solutions business, which has higher margins and greater potential,” he said.The incident stems from a key-generation process conducted on April 30, 2025. Srinivasan said delays in procuring hardware for North American operations meant the company had to generate keys in India and subsequently export them. A script error resulted in weak keys, while inadequate maker-checker controls contributed to the problem.“It was a script error and human error,” he said, adding that the company would strengthen operational and security controls and review its processes.The company said it revoked the affected intermediate certificate authorities within 14 hours of discovering the issue and disclosed it promptly. Chairman V Srinivasan said the incident did not involve a compromise of the company’s infrastructure or a data breach, and that physical and logical security controls remained intact.The incident has also affected customers relying on eMudhra’s G3 root, a top-level certificate authority that helps browsers establish trust in digital certificates used to authenticate websites and secure connections.Kaushik Srinivasan said around 30,000 certificates associated with the G3 root were affected after it was distrusted, and the company was working to transition them. One customer in North America was impacted, he said.The company is working with browser programmes and customers to manage the transition. It plans to replace affected certificates and use alternative providers where required, while seeking to minimise disruption to customer-facing services.“Our G1 root, as I understand it, continues to be trusted,” Srinivasan said, adding that the company was also working to transition customers covered by the G1 root. The company has said its G1 RSA roots will continue to serve customers until the transition is complete and that replacement certificates will be provided free of cost through partners.Srinivasan said the company would commission an independent review by an empanelled auditor to examine its cryptographic keys, key inventories and key-generation processes. The findings will be made public, he said.eMudhra plans to focus on its other businesses, including digital signature certificates, eSign, enterprise public key infrastructure platforms, its emSigner eSignature Suite, and identity and authentication solutions. The company said these operations run on infrastructure separate from its global SSL/TLS business and remain unaffected.While the direct revenue contribution from SSL/TLS is small, Srinivasan said the company was also seeking to contain the reputational risk arising from the incident and restore customer confidence.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), in an advisory issued on Wednesday, said eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities were affected by a key-generation flaw that resulted in weak cryptographic private keys.You use AI every day. articles.title: Elon Musk makes $1 billion investment in Ellison’s Skydance
articles.summary: Skydance has tapped equity investments from an array of sources, including Middle East sovereign wealth funds.
articles.body:
Elon Musk has invested roughly $1 billion in Skydance, according to people familiar with the matter, providing a much needed financial injection as the company looks to cut costs and bolster its stock price.

The deal came together at roughly the same time as equity investments from Skydance's other investors, including board member Laurene Powell Jobs, the people said. Semafor reported in September that Paramount was considering seeking an equity injection from Musk.

Musk has publicly praised the Ellisons and Skydance, prompting speculation of a more expansive partnership between Musk's lower-earth-orbit satellite network, Starlink, and Skydance.

"He's gonna have to re-engineer all of those channels, and figure out how they morph into streams themselves rather than just traditional linear," billionaire cable executive John Malone said Tuesday. "I think there's a deal coming there," Malone also said at his Paley Center appearance .

"Who helped Elon finance Twitter when he bought it? Larry Ellison," Malone said. "How did Larry Ellison come up with some of the money to put into the creation of Skydance? Tesla stock. And I would not doubt for a minute that before very long you're going to see an announcement."

A deal, in fact, had already come. Ellison, who poached Mattel's Ynon Kreiz to serve as co-CEO, could use Musk's capital to bolster the company's cost-cutting and technological efforts.

"We are building a true product and tech team," Ellison said in a CNBC interview earlier this month. "We are a big believer that artificial intelligence is a tool for artists, not the other way around."

Musk and Paramount did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Musk was among a number of wealthy individuals that Paramount CEO David Ellison was considering working with for an investment.

Musk and David Ellison's father, Oracle founder Larry Ellison, have long been close, and it is in part the elder Ellison's money — and connections — that made Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros. possible. Larry Ellison has personally guaranteed more than $40 billion of the equity financing for Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros.

Larry Ellison invested $1 billion in Musk's 2022 deal to take X, formerly Twitter, private. He also invested in Tesla in 2018, and served on the company's board of directors for years.

articles.title: Big companies are rethinking 'out of control' AI spending — and turning to cheaper models
articles.summary: Companies are watching their artificial intelligence spending, and the big AI developers are catering to that.
articles.body:
IBM ( IBM ) is calling attention to a growing trend among companies and their AI spending: They're keeping a closer eye on it.

"I think what we are seeing is that at least larger enterprises are becoming a lot more cognizant and a lot more aware of what the true ROI of all of their AI spend is," IBM CEO Arvind Krishna said during the tech company's earnings call on Wednesday.

"They are also getting worried if some of the AI spending is completely out of control with no real return," he added.

While hyperscalers have been ramping up capital spending on AI infrastructure and data centers, enterprise customers are increasingly turning to open-weight models , whose core components are public, as a more cost-effective way to implement AI.

"Our computation is that for an average large enterprise, you can get going with maybe two or three racks [of infrastructure]," said Krishna. "It gives you the ability to run those open-weight models currently, anywhere from 25% to 10% of the token cost of the frontier models."

Krishna noted that IBM's on-premises IT infrastructure is well-positioned for the shift, enabling the protection of intellectual property by running models locally or on private clouds.

Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk recently argued that the key metric defining the AI build-out isn't physical capacity or power, but the price customers are willing to pay for the computing power being built. The costs of AI tokens have also fallen sharply.

(Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

Companies are willing to pay a premium for computing power if it helps them increase revenue, improve profit margins, or cut costs. But those benefits have yet to materialize at a meaningful scale, Sløk has argued.

Frontier AI developers OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) and Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) are responding to enterprise demand for more affordable models.

OpenAI introduced lower-cost mid-range additions to its GPT-6 model family in September. Earlier this month, Anthropic unveiled Claude Haiku 5.5 , promising better performance at a lower cost than its predecessor.

Anthropic is on the march toward its highly anticipated initial public offering IPO w ith an S-1 filing potentially dropping as soon as Friday.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq tumble as oil climbs, investors weigh Meta, Tesla earnings

articles.body: US stocks fell on Thursday, led by the Tech (XLK) sector as the AI trade unwound and Wall Street assessed earnings from EV maker Tesla (TSLA) and social media giant (META). Investors flocked to bonds, sending Treasury yields lower as oil prices surged to a five-month high.The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) declined 0.2%, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC) fell 1.2%. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) tumbled 2.1% as semicondcutor stocks fell, reversing gains from Wednesday's session. Tesla shares were volatile after an earnings beat, as investors weighed lower 2026 capex against higher spending in 2027 and 2028 on Optimus, Cybercab, and Terafab. SpaceX (SPCX) stock fell, giving back more than half of Wednesday's post-earnings gain.Meanwhile, Blackstone's (BX) stock climbed 5% after the firm offered an upbeat outlook for its upcoming investment sales. A report that the US and Israel are preparing for renewed attacks on Iran after the US mid-term elections sent Brent crude (BZ=F) to $112 per barrel while West Texas Intermediate crude (CL=F) climbed to $100. A deadly attack at a Saudi Arabian airport and oil field also put upward pressure on energy prices. In other news, jobless claims fell to 194,000 last week, the fewest in three months, underscoring how layoffs remain low.

articles.title: Dollar General agrees to nearly $1.9m settlement for overcharging New York customers
articles.summary: Government inspections showed overcharges as high as 39% on some items. The discount store giant was the subject of a 2025 investigation by the Guardian
articles.body:
Dollar General, the nation's largest dollar-store chain, has agreed to a $1.875m deal to settle allegations that it "repeatedly and persistently" overcharged customers across New York state.

The New York attorney general's office found that Dollar General often charged customers higher prices at checkout than the prices it promised on shelf labels, signs, advertising circulars and its mobile app. The state agency said one check of 114 items across multiple stores revealed overcharges on individual items as high as 26%, 38% and 39%.

Under the settlement, Dollar General will donate $1.875m in food and personal items to a regional food bank in upstate New York. The agreement also requires that the company put in place comprehensive price-accuracy safeguards at its more than 600 stores statewide.

"When New Yorkers see a sale price advertised on the shelf, they should be able to trust that they'll be charged that same price at the register," the New York attorney general, Letitia James, said.

The pricing issues at the company – which promotes itself as "a lifeline for affordable, everyday essentials" – are not limited to the state of New York.

A Guardian investigation published in December reported that the chain frequently overcharged customers across the nation for such items as Flintstones vitamins, Peter Pan peanut butter and Prego pasta sauce. Dollar General stores flunked more than 4,300 government price-accuracy inspections in 23 states between 2022 and 2025, the Guardian found.

An inspection at a Dollar General in Port Henry, New York, for example, flagged overcharges on 78% of the items checked.

Under the terms of the New York settlement, the company will be required to embrace a long list of policies and procedures – including scheduling staff to ensure shelf tags are updated for pricing accuracy and hiring independent auditors to conduct secret shopper tests.

The company will also be required to reformat its receipts. State investigators found Dollar General's receipts included "various confusing formats" that made it difficult for consumers to figure out what they were really paying.

Dollar General neither admitted nor denied New York authorities' findings.

In a statement in response to questions from the Guardian, it said: "Dollar General is committed to providing customers with accurate on-shelf prices on items purchased in our stores, and we are disappointed any time we fail to deliver on this commitment. When a pricing discrepancy is identified, our store teams are instructed, expected and empowered to correct the matter on the spot for our customers."

It added that "we have in place a number of measures designed to promote pricing accuracy, and we continuously evaluate and evolve these measures".

articles.title: Ultraviolette eyes Europe expansion with Venom launch
articles.summary: Ultraviolette launches X-47 Venom e-motorcycle, eyes Europe expansion with EICMA debut; targets 1,000 monthly bike sales by Q1 2027 and more capacity.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Ultraviolette on Thursday launched its X-47 Venom electric motorcycle as it prepares to expand its European presence and increase monthly motorcycle sales from around 700 to 1,000 in the first quarter of 2027.The Bengaluru-based company will introduce the Venom in Europe on Nov 3 at the EICMA motorcycle exhibition in Milan. It already exports to 20 European countries, including Germany, France, Italy and the UK. Europe accounts for roughly 10% of its current sales, the company said.The Venom is priced at Rs 2.6 lakh, ex-showroom Bengaluru, for the first 5,000 customers. The starting price will rise to Rs 3 lakh thereafter. Bookings opened on Thursday. The model is an updated version of the X-47 Crossover.The launch comes as Ultraviolette broadens its product portfolio, expands its distribution network and adds manufacturing capacity. Beyond Europe, it plans to enter the US in 2027 and is exploring opportunities in Latin America and Southeast Asia.Domestic expansion will accompany the overseas push. CEO and co-founder Narayan Subramaniam told reporters on Thursday that the company plans to expand its retail network from around 50 locations to 100 by the first quarter of 2027. With additional products, including the Shockwave motorcycle and Tesseract scooter, it is targeting sales of around 10,000 vehicles a month by this time next year.This broader target goes beyond the near-term increase expected from its motorcycle business as the company prepares to enter the electric scooter market. The planned additions will expand its portfolio across sports, crossover and street-and-dirt motorcycles, as well as scooters.Ultraviolette raised $85 million in September in a funding round led by Yali Capital and TDK Ventures, with participation from Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan. The funds are intended to support manufacturing capacity, new electric vehicle platforms and international expansion.The company has also announced plans to invest Rs 779 crore over five years in a new factory in Hosur, Tamil Nadu. The facility is designed to ramp up to an annual capacity of 2.5 lakh vehicles in phases. It will manufacture the Tesseract scooter and future products, alongside the company’s existing Bengaluru operations.The Venom is the first motorcycle built on Ultraviolette’s VX-100 platform, which combines new battery, motor and control systems. The architecture can accommodate different battery capacities and power outputs, allowing the company to extend it across future models and markets.Subramaniam described VX-100 as establishing “a technology foundation for a new generation of products across segments and markets”. The company developed the platform as it prepared to expand beyond its existing motorcycle portfolio.Founded in 2016 by Subramaniam and Niraj Rajmohan, Ultraviolette counts TVS Motor, Qualcomm Ventures, Zoho and Lingotto among its investors. Its existing motorcycle portfolio includes the F77 range and X-47 Crossover.(With inputs from agencies)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Bond traders are backing off Fed rate hike bets — here's what it means for mortgage rates
articles.summary: Bonds are rallying despite $110 oil — the 10-year yield is on track for its biggest drop in two years.
articles.body:
If oil is about to spark an inflation wave, the bond market hasn't heard about it.

Brent crude ( BZ=F ) is trading around $112 a barrel, more than 50% higher than before the Iran war began in late February. Normally, that kind of spike would have bond investors worried about inflation and pushing interest rates higher.

Instead, Treasurys are rallying on Thursday as stocks slide. The 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ) is on track for its biggest one-day drop in more than two years, slipping back below 5%. When bond prices rise, yields fall. That matters for anyone shopping for a home, because mortgage rates tend to follow the 10-year .

Behind the move is a quick change of heart about the Federal Reserve as long-term interest rates decline. The Fed meets next week, on Oct. 28, and investors have been bracing for it to raise rates to fight perceived oil-driven inflation.

Those bets are fading fast. Fed funds futures now put the odds of an October hike at about 5%, according to Bloomberg data. That's down from 15% on Wednesday and 37% at the end of September.

The outlook for December has shifted too. As recently as Wednesday, traders were fully priced for a hike by year-end. Now they see roughly a 75% chance.

Why bond traders aren't panicking about oil

Even with oil soaring, the bond market's inflation forecast has barely budged.

One way to measure what investors expect is the gap between regular Treasurys and Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities, or TIPS , which pay extra when prices rise. That gap, called the breakeven rate , says investors expect inflation to average about 2.4% a year over the next five years. That's the same as before the war started.

So why did yields climb so much this year? Almost all of it came from "real" yields, which is what bonds pay after inflation. That's a bet the Fed will keep rates high enough to stop oil from turning into lasting inflation, not a bet that inflation is about to take off.

Not everyone buys the market's calm. Bloomberg strategist Simon White argues breakevens are "mispricing" the oil shock.

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate fell to 7.32% this week from 7.40%, according to Freddie Mac. That's the first drop in two months, after a seven-week climb that took rates to their highest level since 2023. Before the war, rates were just under 6%.

Freddie Mac's survey doesn't capture Thursday's bond rally. If yields stay lower, mortgage rates could follow in the coming days.

articles.title: Hooters restaurants keep shuttering - but the CEO calls it a comeback
articles.summary: The company has more than 420 restaurants in 29 countries
articles.body:
Hooters restaurants are closing left and right but the CEO insists the iconic brand is making a comeback.

A group of six businessmen, who founded Hooters in Clearwater, Florida, in 1983, recently reacquired the restaurant chain after the previous owners, Hooters for America, filed for bankruptcy in 2025.

The sports bar, known for its chicken wings and female servers in revealing uniforms, is undergoing a review of its operations and remaining locations.

"It's going to take some time," CEO Neil Kiefer recently told Fox News. "Change the culture. Get the menu right. Get the uniform right. And get the physical [store] plans right."

The chain will roll out its signature buffalo wing sauce at all U.S. restaurants and have hospitality training for hosts and hostesses, Kiefer said.

The company, which has more than 420 locations in 29 countries, has closed numerous restaurants in the year since the original owners took over.

Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, and New York no longer have Hooters locations , according to The Street . At least three long-standing Florida locations have shuttered this year, according to Fox News :

Jacksonville: Closed in October after 40 years

Panama City Beach: Closed in September after more than three decades

Boca Raton: Closed in February after 16 years.

Hooters is one of several well-known chains announcing closures this year.

True Food Kitchen, a restaurant backed by Oprah Winfrey, declared bankruptcy and shuttered 12 locations in October . An Applebee's franchisee that owns more than 50 restaurants filed for bankruptcy in March .

Fast-food brands are feeling the sting of fading consumer spending, too. Wendy's announced in May it was closing hundreds of restaurants after faltering sales across the U.S. Pizza Hut announced in February it was closing 250 locations across the U.S. amid a strategic review.

Consumers are cutting their dining out budgets as inflation rises and the cost of everyday essentials become more expensive.

This year, some 39 percent of adults reported eating out at least once a week - down from 47 percent in 2022 and 59 percent in 2019, according to a new Gallup survey .

Total restaurant spending has remained flat for the past three years , according to an August analysis from think tank Center for Economic Policy and Research.

That trend might continue for a few years, McDonald's CEO Chris Kempczinski said during a CNBC interview last month.

"We're not expecting that the industry all of a sudden is going to go to having robust traffic growth - we think that's going to be largely flat," he said.

articles.title: Oil Futures For 2027 Have Jumped Almost 20%. Traders Believe Relief Could Take Longer Than Expected.
articles.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration has raised its oil price forecasts, adding to concerns about borrowing costs, consumer spending and the outlook fo...
articles.body:
Oil traders are increasingly betting that high energy costs will persist well into 2027, with crude futures for delivery next year rising sharply since September as the Middle East war disrupts global supplies.

West Texas Intermediate futures for January 2027 delivery reached $97.10 a barrel this week. June contracts have jumped 18% to around $88, while December futures have climbed 13% to about $81, according to FactSet market data.

The increases suggest traders expect oil to remain expensive for longer than they anticipated just weeks ago, although futures prices are not guarantees of what crude will cost when those contracts expire.

The latest figures from the International Energy Agency show the extent of the pressure on global supplies. Oil inventories were 509 million barrels below their prewar levels at the end of September, with onshore stocks falling by 113 million barrels during the month. An increase in oil held aboard ships partly offset that decline, leaving overall inventories down 10 million barrels.

Middle Eastern oil exports are recovering, but supply constraints remain. Crude shipments from Gulf producers increased by 4.4 million barrels a day in September to 13.9 million barrels, reaching more than 75% of prewar levels.

Saudi Arabia led the recovery, using alternative shipping routes and tanker transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz. However, attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels continue to threaten shipments, while longer routes and higher insurance costs have made transportation more expensive.

The IEA expects global oil demand to decline by 2.6 million barrels a day in 2026 as high prices and weaker economic conditions affect consumption. Even with lower demand, the agency forecasts an oil supply deficit through the end of the year.

The U.S. Energy Information Administration's October Short-Term Energy Outlook also points to higher prices ahead. The agency raised its forecast for average Brent crude prices in 2027 to $84 a barrel, up from $74 in September. It also increased its fourth-quarter 2026 forecast by $14 to $105 a barrel.

Brent averaged $114 in September, compared with $91 in August, and briefly reached $131 on September 15 following an attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline.

The EIA expects prices to ease as regional production and shipping capacity recover, with Brent averaging $87 in the second quarter of 2027 and $74 in the final quarter. However, those projections were based on information available through October 1, before the latest increase in futures prices.

articles.title: Santiago Niño Becerra, economista: "Que la riqueza se iba a concentrar en un puñado de grandes compañías era más que obvio"
articles.standfirst: El catedrático analiza los cambios que provocará la Inteligencia Artificial
articles.summary: El catedrático analiza los cambios que provocará la Inteligencia Artificial
articles.body: El economista Santiago Niño Becerra ha vaticinado cambios profundos en la economía mundial debido a la Inteligencia Artificial. El experto ha destacado la reflexión de un artículo de Business Insider que sostiene que, debido a los oligopolios, desde el sector tecnológico se reclaman mecanismos que garanticen un reparto más justo de la riqueza. Por ejemplo, una renta básica universal para la ciudadanía. En este sentido, Santiago Niño Becerra no se ha mostrado sorprendido por la información que plantea el citado medio. "Que la riqueza se iba a concentrar en un puñado de grandes compañías –oligopolios– era más que obvio y lo hemos comentado en numerosas ocasiones", ha explicado en sus redes sociales. El catedrático catalán ha comentado que, en su opinión, la sociedad mundial está viviendo un episodio similar al de la denominada Edad dorada en Estados Unidos, a finales del siglo XIX: "Protagonizado por sus grandes magnates: Vanderbilt, Rockefeller, Carnegie, J.P. Morgan, Gould, Stanford... Que concentraron inmensos capitales con estructuras oligopolistas apoyados en una estructura política muy peculiar y explotando a una sociedad sumida en una desigualdad absoluta". Santiago Niño Becerra ha señalado una diferencia entre ambas épocas que, según él, es clave. "Entonces ninguno de estos magnates pensó en crear ningún fondo que amortiguase tal desigualdad; hoy sí", ha destacado. La argumentación del economista no invita al optimismo: "Hoy las cosas pueden ser incluso peor que entonces. En mi opinión, excepto en el campo militar, se están diluyendo las consecuencias de la IA". La Inteligencia Artificial provocará en el futuro, según ha comentado el catedrático catalán, "excedentes inmensos de horas de trabajo". Esto es algo que, tal como ha relatado Santiago Niño Becerra, no ocurrió en la Edad dorada de Estados Unidos. El economista, de hecho, ha calificado las pérdidas que ha experimentado Anthropic como "una anécdota en el medio plazo".

articles.title: This level-headed Tesla bull still expects 5 million Cybercabs by 2040
articles.summary: Wall Street continues to bet big on Tesla's Cybercab.
articles.body:
Tesla's ( TSLA ) surprise $5 billion haircut to its capital expenditure plans in its latest earnings call hasn't shaken investor confidence in the long-term potential of a large Cybercab network.

Maybe some near-term confidence was lost in the Optimus humanoid as Tesla deals with design challenges, but not in Cybercabs.

Case in point: Even the reasonable modeling assumptions on the Cybercab from Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco, who has an Equal Weight rating on the stock, still have the fleet size hitting 5 million by the end of 2040. That will be fueled by sharp growth over the next three years, as the chart below indicates.

"Importantly, Tesla is pursuing both geographic expansion and increasing fleet density within existing markets, with plans to expand operating hours toward 24/7 service, higher-speed roads, highways, and more weather conditions by year-end," Percoco said. "In response to our question, management acknowledged that software capabilities remain a constraint on scaling today, although regulatory approvals could become the primary bottleneck over time."

He added, "We continue to view sustained growth in unsupervised miles, fleet density, and safety performance as the most important indicators of progress toward commercial scale. We come away from the quarter more confident in our fleet size estimates through 2027 given the pace of progress demonstrated thus far."

Musk said on Tesla's late Wednesday earnings call that the company's Cybercab fleet in Austin, Texas, has grown by a factor of 10 since its launch roughly a month ago. The company has more than 300 Cybercabs operating in Austin.

Tesla said it has reached nearly 2 million cumulative unsupervised miles for its Cybercab service as of the end of the third quarter. Operating hours in Austin are now 6 a.m. to midnight.

The company plans to expand its Cybercab service to Dallas in November.

articles.title: Investors are punishing Big Tech's biggest spenders. Meta is the latest casualty.
articles.summary: Meta stock is on track for its third straight drop of more than 5% after earnings, a first since its IPO.
articles.body:
Apple ( AAPL ), Eli Lilly ( LLY ), and Walmart ( WMT ) have added more than $400 billion since chip stocks peaked in early October. Meta ( META ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and SpaceX ( SPCX ) have lost more than twice that.

Meta is taking the hardest hit. The stock is down more than 8% on Thursday, erasing about $145 billion in market value and wiping out its gain for the year. It's on track for its second-worst day of 2026 and its third straight drop of 5% or more the day after earnings — a first since its 2012 IPO.

Thursday's drop looks dramatic, but on a weekly chart, it barely registers. For about two years, Meta has bounced between roughly $500 and $800, from its April 2025 low near $485 to its August 2025 record close of $790.

Slipping below the 2025 close turns Meta red for the year. It doesn't change the trend. Only a break out of the box would.

The broader damage is hitting the AI spenders.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) alone has shed more than $600 billion since Oct. 6, according to Yahoo Finance calculations, as chip stocks broke a bear trap .

Meta beat on revenue on Wednesday , with sales up 26% to $64.6 billion. But the company raised its full-year expense outlook and narrowed its capital spending plan to $135 billion to $145 billion. It also unveiled a new class of nonvoting shares it can sell to raise money.

"He's not going to have the cash flow to support it. So he's going to have to raise capital, both debt and equity," Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said to Yahoo Finance in reference to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

Bond traders were already nervous. Earlier this week, the cost of insuring debt from Meta, Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet, and Microsoft ( MSFT ) climbed to its highest in months. Truist analysts wrote that Meta's AI investments "will take longer to generate returns."

The core business is holding up, though. Luria said Meta is "gaining share from Google," with ad sales growing in the 20s. And Zuckerberg told analysts that if compute efficiency keeps improving quickly, "Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years."

Watch for a weekly close outside the box. A move above $800 would be a breakout to new highs, while a close below $500 would open the door to a much deeper slide. Until then, the moves are just noise inside the range.

Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.

Follow Jared Blikre on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com .

articles.title: Meta stock falls 7% as AI spending fears return
articles.summary: Meta stock fell 7% Thursday.
articles.body:
Meta ( META ) stock closed out the trading day Thursday down 7% on, despite reporting better-than-anticipated Q3 revenue results Wednesday, as AI bubble fears remerged across Wall Street.

Investors pulled back on semiconductor and other AI stocks across the board on questions about whether massive investments in AI data centers will pay off in the long run.

Meta raised the lower end of its capital expenditure estimates to between $135 billion and $145 billion from $130 billion and $145 billion. The company also has $825 billion in various spending commitments related to cloud capacity arrangements, energy service agreements, and consumer hardware products.

Despite Wall Street's reaction to Meta's earnings, analysts were largely bullish on the company's outlook, owing to its prospects for its Muse AI agent and models.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg repeatedly pointed to Muse as a source of growth potential during the company's earnings call, saying "Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years," as long as compute efficiency in AI systems continues to improve.

Meta posted an all-time high revenue of $64 billion in the quarter, well ahead of the $63.3 billion analysts anticipated. GAAP earnings per share came in at $3.83 versus expectations of $3.56, but would have been $7.40 without legal charges related to the company's teen mental health settlement.

The company also announced it will issue new non-voting Class C shares to all Class A stockholders , effectively creating a 2-for-1 stock split. The move is meant to ensure Zuckerberg stays in California and retains voting control of the company if the state's Proposition 40 passes on Election Day.

Prop. 40 calls for a 5% tax on taxpayers with assets over $1 billion.

Ahead of Meta's earnings report, a New Mexico judge ordered the company to pay $25 billion in connection with the state's consumer-harms case against the social media giant.

Email Daniel Howley at dhowley@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on Twitter at @DanielHowley .

articles.title: Moderna stock crashes as leaked melanoma data threatens its record August rally
articles.summary: Leaked results from Moderna's melanoma vaccine trial have the stock challenging its worst day ever, while the rest of healthcare rallies.
articles.body:
Two months ago, Moderna's ( MRNA ) melanoma vaccine handed the stock its best day ever. Now leaked results from the same trial have handed it its biggest intraday drop on record.

The stock fell as much as 26% before closing down more than 17%. That's still its worst day since Aug. 20, the session right after its best day.

More than $17 billion in market value has vanished as details from the late-stage trial circulated ahead of their official debut . Merck ( MRK ), Moderna's partner on the vaccine, confirmed the results came out early. The full data is set for release Saturday at Europe's biggest cancer conference, in Madrid.

The leaked numbers are still good. The personalized vaccine, paired with Merck's blockbuster Keytruda, reportedly cut the risk of the cancer returning or death by 42%. An earlier, smaller trial showed 49%, though it used different patients, so it isn't a direct comparison. The bigger issue is how much the stock had already run, nearly quadrupling from mid-August to Wednesday.

Merck fell nearly 4% at its low before paring more than half the drop. The vaccine is central to Moderna's story, but it's just an add-on for Merck.

The rest of healthcare is rallied. Eli Lilly ( LLY ) is added more than $33 billion in market value, about twice what Moderna lost. Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) and Pfizer ( PFE ) rose, too.

The iShares Biotechnology ETF ( IBB ) and SPDR S&P Biotech ETF ( XBI ) were only modestly lower, roughly in step with the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ).

On Aug. 19, Moderna rocketed 177% to close at $174.38 after the company said the trial met its goals. It kept climbing from there, and on Wednesday, it posted its highest close since December 2021.

Thursday's low came within 4% of that August close before buyers stepped in. A sustained break below $174 would put $116 in focus. That's where trading opened on the record day.

Watch Saturday's full data, especially how lower-risk patients fared.

Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com .

articles.title: California's Prop 40: What to know about the billionaire wealth tax
articles.summary: California voters will decide Nov. 3 whether to approve Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state’s billionaires.
articles.body:
The California billionaire tax, Proposition 40, is finally coming to a vote on Nov. 3. The measure would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state's billionaires. Two competing initiatives on the same ballot, Props 41 and 42, are backed by opponents of the tax, including billionaires.

If either garners more yes votes than Prop 40, it could keep the tax from taking effect.

The labor union Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West (SEIU-UHW) is spearheading the campaign for the tax on the state's ultra-wealthy to prevent hospital and clinic closures, protect healthcare jobs, and help fund K-14 public education and state food assistance programs.

Opponents, including Gov. Gavin Newsom, say the tax would fuel an exodus of wealthy company founders and investors, spark job losses, and further weaken California's economy.

Prop 40 would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaire state residents, subject to the asset restrictions noted below. Taxpayers could choose to pay the tax in five annual installments, with a 7.5% annual deferral charge on the unpaid balance.

Billionaire residents in California as of Jan. 1, 2026, would owe the tax in 2027. That's an estimated 255 eligible taxpayers, according to data from Altrata, a wealth-intelligence firm, reported by the Wall Street Journal.

The tax proposal is not based on income — that's a loophole that allows billionaires to pay less in income taxes than the average American . Rather, the proposed California tax is based on billionaires' assets, including equity holdings, often in their own companies. The impact on the most wealthy would vary widely.

A half-dozen or more high-profile billionaires relocated out of state as news of the proposed tax rolled out last year, so the number may be slightly lower.

Those who have reportedly relocated include Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, though neither has said that their moves were related to the possible tax.

A Meta regulatory filing dated Oct. 21 said that founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg told a special board committee that he was considering moving out of the state to avoid the tax if it were passed.

The committee said it was "critically important to keep Mr. Zuckerberg in a leadership position with our Company and that he continue to reside in and manage the Company from our headquarters in California," and approved a special class of stock that he could use to pay any wealth tax due.

The tax's effect would vary widely. The Tax Foundation, a right-leaning tax policy nonprofit, projected that the tax would render Tony Xu, the founder of DoorDash, bankrupt, with a tax liability of $4.17 billion, unless he could challenge the initiative's valuation of his assets.

On the other hand, Jensen Huang of Nvidia would face a tax liability of more than twice that: $8.5 billion. He told Bloomberg that he's fine with that .

The California healthcare worker union, SEIU-UHW, launched the "emergency tax" initiative to offset possible healthcare staffing issues and service reductions at healthcare facilities. The union estimates a nearly $100 billion loss of federal funding over the next five years due to the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

Taxpayers and trusts with assets over $1 billion would be taxed on businesses, securities, collectibles, and intellectual property, but the tax would exclude real property and certain retirement accounts and pensions.

The California Billionaire Tax Act is estimated to raise about $100 billion, according to the initiative's website. The Legislative Analyst's Office, the state's nonpartisan fiscal adviser, estimates that the state would collect tens of billions of dollars from the wealth tax but says the exact amount is harder to predict.

BillionaireTaxNow.org says the money would be used to:

Keep hospitals, ERs, clinics, nursing homes, and home care facilities open and staffed

"Stabilize" healthcare insurance premiums and coverage

Fund K-14 public education programs and staffing

Fund California food assistance programs

Arguments in favor of the California billionaire tax

The Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy, a left-leaning think tank, supports the California billionaire tax, saying that the One Big Beautiful Bill Act "cut health care and food support in part to pay for tax cuts for the very wealthiest Americans. The legislation gives more than $1 trillion in tax savings to the richest 1% of households over the next decade."

ITEP added in the analysis that, "ultra-wealthy households have many ways to enjoy a lavish lifestyle without selling most of their holdings, and so can largely avoid the individual income tax. The billionaire tax directly remedies this injustice by taxing all wealth, whether this wealth has been realized as income or not."

Arguments against the California billionaire tax

The Tax Foundation believes the California billionaire tax, as drafted, contains "aggressive design choices and possible drafting errors" that could result in the proposed one-time 5% tax being "dramatically higher."

It warns that "the poorly drafted initiative" could force company founders to sell "a significant portion" of their shares and lose their controlling interests. Stock prices could plunge, impacting retirement savings and investment account balances of working Americans.

The Hoover Institution, a right-leaning think tank, has said the wealth tax would leave California about $25 billion worse off, accounting for lost income tax revenue from billionaires leaving the state. It also estimated revenues from the levy would fall short of the $100 billion projection, more likely generating just $40 billion.

What about federal wealth tax proposals?

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) has long advocated for a national wealth tax. His "Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act," co-sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), was introduced in March.

The national tax would levy a 5% annual, not one-time, tax on the estimated 938 billionaires in the U.S., estimated to raise $4.4 trillion over the next 10 years. In the first year, the bill would give a $3,000 payment to "every man, woman, and child" in a household earning $150,000 or less.

The bill moved to committees in both the Senate and House, where no further action was taken.
